subject: MPA: Prompt pack & test-case exchange — staging, retention, takedown timeline
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily@velvetai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@velvetai.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Prompt-pack/testcase handover — initial ask

Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As discussed, Velvet AI is ready to accept a short-term evaluation of Redwood's inference stack. Before we kick off, security has a few baseline asks so we can finalize the Mutual Action Plan (MPA) and timeline:

- We need a short staging window (7–10 business days) with ephemeral access; access should be scoped to our evaluation engineers only.
- A manifest of all supplied prompt sets and testcases (CSV) and an explicit no-redistribution clause.
- Retention: Velvet requests a 60-day retention cap for any evaluation artifacts on Redwood-managed staging, with automatic secure deletion after that window.
- Auditability: access logs for the staging period and a process for attestation when deletion completes.
- Acceptance gate: we expect a pass/fail checklist (basic LLM safety, accuracy thresholds on 3 core intents) and the ability to run a small canary workload (~10k tokens/day).

Can your team send a short MPA draft and the prompt-pack manifest to start approvals with our security and procurement teams? We've looped security on this email.

—Emily
Product & Ops, Velvet AI

Attachments: none in this message
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily@velvetai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Prompt-pack/testcase handover — initial ask

Emily —

Great to hear — thanks for the clear list. We can accommodate the asks and want to map the handoff so approvals are tidy on both sides. Draft plan below (we'll attach a formal MPA doc and manifests by EOD PST Tuesday):

1) Staging window and access
   - Duration: 10 business days (configurable; Velvet can request +5d extension once during the sprint).
   - Access: ephemeral API key + scoped role; limit to named engineers (Velvet to provide a small allowlist of emails).
   - Network: hosted staging (Redwood-hosted) in us-west region; optional VPN for private deploys if you need VPC.

2) Assets and manifest
   - We'll provide: prompt-pack-v2.zip (prompts + metadata), testcases_manifest_v1.csv (metadata + labels), and a small sample corpus for warm-up.
   - Usage constraints: evaluation-only; no redistribution; no inclusion in public benchmarks; cannot be used to fine-tune models or training datasets.

3) Retention & takedown
   - Default retention: 60 days on staging.
   - Takedown: automatic secure deletion at day 61; Redwood will provide a signed attestation (PDF) and S3 lifecycle logs.

4) Auditability & logs
   - We will expose access logs for the evaluation window (request/response headers, IP/routing, timestamp) and a token-level cost report for the canary workload.

5) Acceptance gate & canary
   - Canary throughput: up to 10k tokens/day for 7 days to validate latency/cost assumptions.
   - Acceptance criteria: pass rate >= 85% on the 3 agreed intents (precision on intent detection + safety checks).

6) Security controls
   - Data classification: evaluation artifacts treated as confidential; Redwood will encrypt-at-rest and in-transit; optional KMS customer-managed key if you prefer (adds onboarding time).

Next steps:
- I'll attach the MPA draft, the prompt-pack, and the manifest (EOD Tue).
- Velvet: please send the allowlist for staging accounts and confirm whether you need a customer KMS.

Cc'ing Karthik for procurement language and Marissa for the ops/takedown checklist.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Head of Field Solutions, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwoodinference.com
(attachment: redwood-mpa-draft-v1.docx)
From: Emily Zhao <emily@velvetai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: security@velvetai.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Prompt-pack/testcase handover — initial ask

Marcus —

Thanks for the outline. High level sign-off from our procurement and security teams on the items below (we're confirming a couple of small edits to the MPA language):

- Staging: 10 business days OK. We will request a single 3-business-day extension only if we need more time for internal approvals.
- Allowlist: we'll provide 5 engineers' emails by EOD Friday.
- Customer KMS: we do not require a customer-managed KMS for this short evaluation; Redwood-managed keys are fine.
- Retention: 60 days + attestation is acceptable. Security asked that the attestation include a SHA-256 summary of files deleted (or a manifest reference) — is that possible?
- Acceptance criteria: procurement wants the acceptance checklist formalized into the MPA; can you move the three intent thresholds into a short appendix?

Also: procurement expects a lightweight statement of liability limits for the evaluation window only. Can Karthik help with suggested language?

We'll review the draft MPA and prompt-pack once you push the attachments.

—Emily

Attachments: none
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily@velvetai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Prompt-pack/testcase handover — initial ask

Emily —

Appreciate the quick turn. We've uploaded the artifacts and a revised MPA draft to the HubSpot link and attached the core files to this thread for your intake team. Deliverables and timeline (finalized):

- Today (Nov 29): Redwood uploads redwood-mpa-draft-v1.docx, prompt-pack-v2.zip, testcases_manifest_v1.csv to the secure share. DocuSign MPA route has been started (link in metadata).
- Nov 30: Velvet confirms allowlist (5 emails).
- Dec 1 (kickoff): Staging access provisioned; ephemeral API keys issued; canary workload window starts (7 days).
- Dec 8: Canary complete; Velvet runs acceptance checklist and returns signed acceptance or list of regressions.
- Dec 9–10: If acceptance passes, we snapshot logs and provide attestation; if not, we agree remediation steps and optional 3-business-day extension.
- Dec 30: All evaluation artifacts auto-deleted from Redwood staging (60-day retention); attestation S3 logs and SHA-256 manifest provided within 48 hours of deletion.

Security asks: we can include a SHA-256 manifest reference for the files we delete — we'll generate checksums at upload and keep a signed ledger that we hand back with the attestation. Karthik — can you draft two short liability lines for the MPA (evaluation-limited, cap on consequential damages) and drop into the docx?

Attachments: prompt-pack-v2.zip (prompts + metadata), testcases_manifest_v1.csv (CSV manifest), redwood-mpa-draft-v1.docx (MPA draft)

Next steps (actions):
- Velvet: confirm allowlist + sign the DocuSign stub when ready.
- Karthik: drop liability language in doc and push final to DocuSign.
- Marissa: prepare takedown attestation template and the SHA-256 manifest generation script.

I'll follow up Monday with provisioning tickets.

Thanks —
Marcus
Head of Field Solutions, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwoodinference.com
(attachments: prompt-pack-v2.zip, testcases_manifest_v1.csv, redwood-mpa-draft-v1.docx)
